note:
The household of Charles Bradley, retired surgeon, a single man with three servants, at 3 Park Terrace (#243) on the 1891 return, transcribed by A. Hagues. None of the four was in the record, and 3 Park Terrace held only 1921, so 1891 is free.

This file replaces an earlier draft of the same name. That draft held Alfred Bradley's household, which was sent as 3 Park Terrace but belongs to Broxtowe House, Park Terrace; A. Hagues corrected it, and it now has a file of its own. Charles Bradley is the man the directory means: Wright's Directory of Nottingham prints 'Mr. Charles Bradley' at 3 Park Terrace in 1894-95 and 1898-99, three and seven years after this return.

**Number 3 passes from one Bradley to another.** Charles is here in 1891 and in the directory to 1898-99; by 1910-11 the directory prints 'Bradley Herbert' at the same number, through 1913-14 and 1915-16, and the record already holds Herbert Bradley (#1796, born 1848) there on the 1921 return. Alfred Bradley, next door but one at Broxtowe House in 1891, is a third man of the same surname and generation. The three are very likely brothers, but no census or directory entry says so, so no family links are made and none of them is bound to another.

Clementina Stimson was born at Wymondham in Leicestershire, as was Julia Rippin, the housekeeper two doors along at 4 Park Terrace in the same year; it is noted as it stands, with nothing read into it. Ages are as the enumerator wrote them, so a birth year worked back from one may be a year out either way.
source: 1891 census, 3 Park Terrace, transcribed by A. Hagues. Directory evidence: Wright's Directory of Nottingham 1894-95, page 107 (Leicester Special Collections id 164613); 1898-99, page 115 (id 165291).
